messages:
alex: Heads-up: saw two prod OOMs in the kv-cache pool (group-7) over the last 6h. Both during very long user contexts (~90k-130k tokens). kernel-selection switched to quant-kernel then spillback, but OOM still hit.
priya: ouch. any repro or traces?
alex: attaching the short summary below — full pprof saved to s3 (s3://redwood-kv-traces/2812345678). quick snippet: 
```
kv_total_alloc: 16.4GB
kv_active: 14.8GB
slab_frag: 41%
reuse_hits (last 1h): 3.2%
paging_events: 124
spillbacks: 2 (both during kernel-switch)
```
marco: that slab_frag number is the smoking gun. long contexts + our sticky-slot policy = fragmentation over time. reuse hits so low means we aren't getting prefix locality.
liz: Were we doing any aggressive prefetch/retention for long sessions? batching heuristics could be holding slots longer than necessary.
alex: batching config on those hosts: max_batch_tokens=2048, batch_window_ms=120, sticky_slot_ttl=30m. Users sending long continuous chats, so sticky_slot_ttl is keeping fragments around.
simone: kernel selection side: we pick quant-kernel for reduced RAM, then kernel-switch tries fallback to float kernel when kv usage spikes. but when we switch, we briefly double memory (kernel A + kernel B caches) which likely pushed it over.
priya: ah that transient peak during switch explains it. we should avoid dual-kernel residency during runtime switch.
marco: mitigation ideas (short list):
- reduce sticky_slot_ttl for long-session namespaces to 2m
- enable incremental kernel handoff (streamed migration) to avoid double residency
- add a hard headroom reserve for kv to refuse new long-context attaches (early 503)
- fallback policy: route to quant-small model variant when kv memory > 75%
liz: also: evict oldest prefix fragments instead of random slab reclaim. priority should be based on reuse_score + age.
alex: agreed. i'm proposing immediate emergency patch: 
1) change sticky_slot_ttl to 2m for group-7 (hotfix)
2) enable kv-evict-oldest=true on the eviction policy
3) add a short-term throttle: reject attachments larger than 50k tokens with 429 + Retry-After
I'll open a canary rollout.
simone: for kernel-switch problem, i'll PR small change to disable keeping both kernels resident during live switch (will try streamed copy). low-risk flag: disable-dual-kernel=true.
priya: Good. Also add metric alarms for dual_residency_memory and slab_fragmentation_ratio > 30%. Set pager if > 45% for 5m.
deploy-bot: deploy started: canary hosts group-7a (3 hosts) with kv-evict-oldest=true, sticky_slot_ttl=120s. release: 2026.3.1-hotfix-kv.
marco: after canary, we should run a synthetic long-context load: 1k sessions with mean 80k tokens, see reuse hits and paging_events. use perf-script in infra repo: 
```
./tools/loadgen --sessions 1000 --mean-tokens 80000 --target group-7a
```
liz: also capture kernel residency timeline with the new flag so we can ensure no overlap. pprof before/after.
alex: initial canary results: paging_events dropped from 124->18 in 30m, slab_frag down from 41%->28%, reuse_hits up to 9.8%. no OOMs so far.
simone: great. kernel-switch PR merged to draft; will run CI and then canary in 2h.
priya: put a short-term playbook note in incidents channel: if OOMs return, immediate steps: 1) enable kv-evict-oldest on all pools, 2) set sticky_slot_ttl=60s globally, 3) scale group capacity by +20% (spawn new instances), 4) temporarily reject new long-attach (>50k) sessions.
marco: long-term: revisit batching heuristics — lower batch_window_ms under high-kv-usage and prefer token-aware batching (max_tokens_per_batch) to avoid holding slots for long windows. also consider per-namespace KV quotas.
liz: log snippets for the incident saved to s3 and linked in the incident ticket (INC-2026-481). Adding small eval to check output quality if we route to quant-small variant.
alex: action items:
- simone: kernel-switch streaming (PR, eta 24h)
- marco: batch heuristics proposal + perf tests (ETA 48h)
- priya: alarms + playbook update (ETA 3h)
- liz: incident ticket + output-quality eval for fallback variant (ETA 8h)
I'll follow up here with monitoring links.
priya: one more: add a soft-degrade response mode where we keep the session but truncate old prefixes client-side (send a warning to client). less user-visible than denying attach.
alex: good UX tradeoff. implement in short-term as an option on the host: kv-trim-old-prefix=true which sends event to session manager.
deploy-bot: canary complete: no regressions, rolling to group-7 (6 hosts).
marco: monitoring dashboard snapshots look good. i'll run the 24h synthetic test overnight and post results.
liz: closing here for now, reopen if OOMs reappear. :thumbsup:
